contract.status: PB1 neutral contract; planned experimental work; not ratified; not part of Brontide Base
decisions: open-decisions.md Decision 1 (2026-07-24): deterministic CBOR core is the portable wire
open-decisions.md Decision 2 (2026-07-24): copied immutable blob is the referenced-resource v0.1 floor

representations.role: The portable wire representation for the negotiated process realization.
Retained diagnostic and legacy representation from the Cooling and Catalog experiments. It is not the portable wire contract and carries no golden byte form.
representations.retiredFrom: portable conformance; see plan section 5 PB4

deterministicCborCore.basis: RFC 8949 section 4.2.1 core deterministic encoding requirements

recordedDecisionRefinement.recordedShorthand: Decision 1 records 'major types 0-5 only ... scalars -> native CBOR (uint/nint/bytes/text/bool/null)'.
recordedDecisionRefinement.refinement: Booleans and null are CBOR major type 7 simple values, and the allowlisted Decimal tag is major type 6. The shorthand therefore describes the structural types; the exact permitted head set is enumerated below. This refinement is recorded rather than left as an implicit codec choice, per plan section 5 PB0 exit.

permittedMajorTypes.name: map
permittedMajorTypes.constraint: definite length only; sorted, unique keys

forbidden.what: half, single, and double floats (major 7, additional info 25, 26, 27)
map keys not in ascending deterministic order
trailing bytes after the top-level item within one frame

argumentEncoding.rule: An argument below 24 is encoded in the additional-info bits; otherwise the smallest of the 1-, 2-, 4-, or 8-byte forms that represents it exactly is used.

mapKeyOrdering.rule: Map entries are sorted in ascending bytewise lexicographic order of the complete deterministic encoding of each key.
mapKeyOrdering.note: Because keys in this contract are text strings, a shorter key sorts before a longer one whenever their length-prefix bytes differ. This is the RFC 8949 core-deterministic rule, not plain string ordering.
mapKeyOrdering.divergenceFromExperiments: The Cooling JSON codec sorts record fields by ordinal string comparison. Ordinal string order and deterministic key order differ once key lengths cross an encoding-width boundary, so PB2 and PB3 must re-sort rather than reuse the existing comparer.

tagAllowlist.name: decimal fraction
tagAllowlist.body: array of exactly two integers: [exponent, mantissa]
canonicalization: exponent and mantissa are each encoded as shortest-form major type 0 or 1.
The mantissa is normalized so that it is not divisible by 10, so one value has exactly one encoding.
The single exception is a zero mantissa, which is encoded as exponent 0 and mantissa 0.

valueEncoding.rule: The negotiated Shape determines the type of every position, so values carry no kind discriminator on the wire. This is the difference from the retained inline-tagged-json representation, whose values are self-describing.

mapping.encoding: simple 21 for true, simple 20 for false
major 0 when the value is >= 0, major 1 otherwise
major 4 array in declared item order
mapping.note: Sequence order is semantic and is never re-sorted.

mapping.encoding: major 4 array of exactly two items: [alternative name as text, alternative value]
major 4 array of exactly two items: [fields map, fragments map]

fieldsMap.absentOptional: An optional field carrying no value is omitted from the map rather than encoded as null. Omission is what makes additive projection possible.

fragmentsMap.keys: the canonical text form '<name>@<version>' of the Fragment reference
fragmentsMap.values: a map of that Fragment's fields, using the same field rules
fragmentsMap.empty: A record with no attached Fragments encodes an empty map (0xa0).
fragmentsMap.rationale: Fields and Fragments occupy two positions of a fixed-length array rather than sharing one map, so no reserved key can collide with a declared field name.

framing.rule: Each frame is a 4-byte big-endian unsigned length prefix followed by exactly that many bytes of deterministic CBOR.

violations.what: a prefix declaring more than maximumBodyBytes
a stream ending before the declared body length

framing.supersedes: The line-delimited framing of the Cooling and Catalog experiments, which remains available only for the diagnostic inline-tagged-json representation.

referencedShapedResource.decision: Decision 2 (2026-07-24): copied immutable blob is the v0.1 floor; the Catalog addressing-only handle is retained as a second proven flavor.
referencedShapedResource.rule: A referenced resource is usable only when the Binding Plan declares a flavor that both endpoints negotiated. An undeclared or unnegotiated flavor is refused visibly and never reported as successful negotiation.

flavors.representation: octet-stream carrying the declared content Shape
flavors.ownershipRule: The receiver obtains an independent immutable copy. There is no borrow interval and the sender retains its own copy.
flavors.releaseRule: Because ownership is by copy, no release or completion signal is required and none is defined. A frame carrying a release signal for this flavor is 'state-violation'.
flavors.fallbackRule: An endpoint that cannot accept this representation fails negotiation with 'unsupported-contract'. There is no implicit conversion and no silent downgrade.

copyAccounting.rule: The copy count is a required C9 observation, so a forbidden implicit copy is visible rather than inferred.

flavors.role: Retained from the Catalog experiment; the only referenced-resource form with existing evidence.
flavors.representation: structured handle with exactly the fields 'provider' and 'id', both Text
flavors.accessRule: The handle conveys addressing and never authority. Possession of a handle is not an admission decision; the provider domain still performs its own admission.
flavors.acceptanceRule: The Binding Plan declares the accepted handles. A handle outside that set is refused before any provider effect.

refusalOutcome.rationale: The Catalog experiment reports the local code 'resource-refused'. Per CH-14 local code strings stay non-normative, so the portable category is the taxonomy value: the resource sits in a declared payload position and cannot conform.
refusalOutcome.notAuthority: The refusal is not 'invalid-authority-presentation'. A handle carries no authority, so refusing one is a payload decision, not an authority decision.

nonGoals.reason: Decision 2 defers borrow-interval, lifetime, and release semantics past 0.1.
Decision 2 defers ownership transfer, reclaim-on-failure, and completion signalling past 0.1.

forbiddenImplicitCopy.rule: A realization may not silently materialize a copy that the declared flavor does not permit. The addressing-only handle permits no copy at all, so producing resource octets for it is 'invalid-payload' with zero provider effects.
